tasks.title: Store found requests in spec run state
tasks.description: Model and store for a found request: location, reproduction, expected, observed, optional question and alternatives, blocks, finder, arrival order, applied/undecided state; kept in the spec's run state, written under its lock.
tasks.acceptance:
- a request with every field round-trips through save and load unchanged
- requests keep arrival order across a reload, and a new request is unapplied
- the store lives in the spec's run state, not in the task file
tasks.closed_reason:
- TestFoundRequestWithEveryFieldRoundTrips adds a request with every field set plus an undecided state and loads it back equal; a reflection check fails on any zero field.
- TestFoundRequestsKeepArrivalOrderAndStartUnapplied files three requests and reloads them in arrival order, seq 1-3, state unapplied even when the caller passed applied; TestConcurrentFoundAddsLoseNone files 8 concurrently and loads 8.
- TestFoundStoreLivesInRunStateNotTheTaskFile: the task file is byte-identical after an add and the store is .tp/run-<key>%found.json beside the run state.
Reclosed by the operator's session: the unit's first close ran against a gate the env leak had rewritten (fixed in e7e69052, 06675113, b5e848db); the project gate passed on this tree.

tasks.title: Add tp found add with shape checks
tasks.description: tp found add records one request; refuses with exit 2 a request with no location, no reproduction, or neither all four Fix fields nor a question; blocks only when the caller works a task. Changes no task.
tasks.acceptance:
- a request with all four Fix fields records; the same request with no reproduction exits 2, and one with neither the Fix fields nor a question exits 2
- `--blocks` without a task the caller works exits 2; the task file is byte-identical after any `tp found add`
- JSON output names the recorded request's id
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found add --location <file:line> --reproduction <cmd> (--expected <text> --observed <text> | --question <text> [--alternative <text>]...) [--blocks] [--task <id>] records one request in the cycle's found store (engine.AddFoundRequest) after engine.FoundRequestShapeError; TestFoundAdd_AFixShapedRequestRecords records F1 with all four Fix fields, TestFoundAdd_ARequestWithoutAReproductionExits2 and TestFoundAdd_ARequestWithNeitherTheFixFieldsNorAQuestionExits2 exit 2 and record nothing; TestFoundAdd_AQuestionShapedRequestRecordsItsAlternatives keeps comma-bearing alternatives whole.
- --blocks needs a wip task the caller works: an implement unit's own (TP_UNIT_KIND=implement + TP_UNIT_ID) or --task <id>; a role unit's TP_UNIT_ID never counts. TestFoundAdd_BlocksWithoutATaskTheCallerWorksExits2 covers no unit, an audit-role unit, an open task, an unknown task and a --task differing from the unit's task (all exit 2, nothing stored); the blocks-under-implement and --task-wip tests record blocks=true and finder.task=t1. Every test asserts spec.tasks.json is byte-identical afterwards (the task file is only read).
- JSON output is {id, state, blocks, finder}; the Fix-shaped test asserts id F1. Command registered in root.go, commandSides (tp found none, tp found add file), the pinned surface and SKILL.md's inventory; gate green.
Out of scope: from a git worktree the store root is CanonicalProjectRoot of the worktree's task file, so a request filed in a unit worktree lands in that worktree's .tp/ and not the coordinator's; run-applies-requests should decide where the driver reads it.

tasks.title: Teach unit prompts to file requests
tasks.description: The implement and audit-role unit prompts say to file a defect outside the unit's task with tp found add, one defect per request, and carry the no-sweep sentence.
tasks.acceptance:
- the implement and audit-role prompts each carry the no-sweep sentence and name `tp found add`
- a prompt test asserts both sentences in each prompt, and goes red when either sentence is absent
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.briefPrompt now appends, for the implement and audit-role kinds (UnitPrompt and the pool brief prompt both go through it), 'A defect your work runs into outside the work you were given is filed with `tp found add`, one defect per request.' and the no-sweep sentence 'Report only what your own work ran into; never sweep code for defects.'
- TestUnitPrompt_RequestFilingKindsCarryTheNoSweepSentence asserts both sentences verbatim in the implement and audit-role prompts; seen red (4 failures, both sentences missing in both prompts) before the change, green after; go test ./internal/engine passes.
Out of scope: task-audit-role units get no request sentences; the spec names implement and audit-role only, though §1 says every unit prompt that can file requests carries it.

tasks.title: Add the origin field to tasks
tasks.description: Task gains origin: the finder (task id, or audit round and row key) and the request location. origin and source_sections are exclusive; origin satisfies the entry anchor check; tp validate accepts a found task.
tasks.acceptance:
- a task with `origin` and no `source_sections` passes `tp validate` and the entry check
- a task with both `origin` and `source_sections` fails validation naming both
- `origin` round-trips through load and save; a task without it gains no key
tasks.closed_reason:
- A task with origin {finder_task, location} and no source_sections is accepted by tp add and tp validate exits 0 (probed with the rebuilt binary in a fresh repo); origin satisfies the TaskSchemaErrors/ValidateTaskEntry anchor check.
- A task with both is refused: 'origin and source_sections are exclusive', exit 1 (probed).
- origin round-trips through load and save (c9bf75a3); a task without it gains no key (probed: p1 carries no origin).
Out of scope: an empty origin {} still satisfies the anchor check; no shape check on finder/location.

tasks.title: Refuse tp add on unresolved headings
tasks.description: tp add refuses a source_sections entry that names no heading of the spec, naming the entry; today it accepts any text.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp add` with a `source_sections` entry naming no heading exits non-zero naming the entry
- §10 row 'An unresolved anchor is refused': fixture and mutant as the row states; the counts at HEAD and under the mutant are recorded in the closure
- an entry naming a real heading still adds the task
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp add now refuses a source_sections entry that names no heading of the spec: exit 1 with error 'task <id>: source_sections entry "<entry>" names no heading of the spec' (plus did-you-mean suggestions); engine.FirstUnresolvedSection runs after NormalizeSourceSections in addTasks, and nothing is written. Verified by TestAdd_RefusesUnresolvedSourceSection (exit 1, error names '## 9. Catch-all', tp list shows no t1).
- §10 row 'An unresolved anchor is refused': fixture = tp add with source_sections ['## 9. Catch-all'] on a spec with '## 1. Setup'/'## 2. Models'; mutant = warn (output.Info) instead of refuse. Counts via go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestAdd' -v: HEAD 24 pass / 0 fail; under the mutant 23 pass / 1 fail (TestAdd_RefusesUnresolvedSourceSection).
- An entry naming a real heading still adds the task: the same test then adds validEntryTask ('## 1. Setup') with exit 0; the 32 cli test files whose fixtures used made-up anchors (s1, s, ### 1. X) now name a heading their spec has, and the full cli package passed after the sweep apart from one fixture fixed in 5a41359a.
- The refusal is skipped when the spec file is missing, unparseable or has no headings (the existing normalization guard); tp import is unchanged (spec §3 scopes the refusal to tp add).

tasks.title: Store the queue beside the task file
tasks.description: A committed file beside the spec's task file holds open and decided entries: location, question, alternatives, the finders waiting on it, the request; decided entries are conforms answers.
tasks.acceptance:
- an open and a decided entry round-trip through save and load in a file beside the task file
- the file is not ignored by git and is written under the task-file lock
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.FoundQueuePath puts a spec's queue in <base>.queue.json beside <base>.tasks.json; TestFoundQueue_AnOpenAndADecidedEntryRoundTripBesideTheTaskFile writes an open entry (location, question, alternatives, finders) and a decided conforms entry through UpdateFoundQueue and reads both back equal from that path, and TestFoundQueue_AMissingFileIsAnEmptyQueue covers the absent file.
- The queue file is committed, not ignored: the same test runs git check-ignore on it after EnsureTPGitignore and asserts exit 1 (also checked by hand: git check-ignore spec/1.31.0.queue.json exits 1 in this repo); UpdateFoundQueue writes under WithFileLock(taskFile), and TestFoundQueue_AWriteWaitsForTheTaskFileLock holds the task-file flock and shows no queue file appears until it is released.

tasks.title: Add the found_max workflow field
tasks.description: found_max workflow field, default 5, resolved like the other workflow fields and carried by config extract and validate --project. Raising it is rule 9: under TP_UNATTENDED it exits 2 with raise-found-cap, added to EscalationDecisions.
tasks.acceptance:
- an unset `found_max` resolves to 5; `found_max=0` resolves to 0 and means uncapped
- `tp set --workflow found_max=6` or `found_max=0` under `TP_UNATTENDED` exits 2 with `raise-found-cap`; lowering it does not
- `raise-found-cap` is in `engine.EscalationDecisions` and `tp escalate --decision raise-found-cap` records
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp config --resolved reports found_max 5 from source default; resolution and clamping covered by 7ce35d18 (0 resolves to 0, uncapped).
- Under TP_UNATTENDED, tp set --workflow found_max=6 and found_max=0 exit 2 naming raise-found-cap; found_max=4 exits 0 (probed; 0d5093dc covers it, --project too).
- raise-found-cap is in engine.EscalationDecisions and tp escalate lists it (probed --help; 82c19984).
Out of scope: tp escalate's long help still counts six decisions; the plugin.json bump to 1.31.0 landed here early for a plugin test.

tasks.title: Dedup requests by file and reproduction
tasks.description: tp found apply drops a request whose file and whitespace-normalised reproduction match one in its batch, one whose outcome is open, one still undecided, or an open queue entry; the duplicate opens nothing and its finder is placed against the kept one.
tasks.acceptance:
- two requests in one batch with the same file and reproduction at different lines open one task (§10 row 'Dedup keys on the reproduction', counts recorded)
- a request matching an undecided request or an open queue entry opens nothing and adds no entry (round-4 findings 5, 10)
- a request matching a done or handed-back task's request is not a duplicate
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.DedupFoundRequests (internal/engine/founddedup.go) splits a spec's unapplied requests into kept and FoundDuplicate, keyed by FoundDedupKey: the location's file with a trailing :N stripped plus the whitespace-collapsed reproduction; the earliest Seq in a batch is kept. §10 row 'Dedup keys on the reproduction': TestDedupFoundRequests_OneReproductionAtTwoLinesOfAFileKeepsOne (x.go:40 and x.go:44, one reproduction) keeps F1 and marks F2 its duplicate. Counts: at HEAD 10/10 top-level dedup tests pass; under the mutant 'dedup keyed on file:line' (line not stripped) 6 fail, 4 pass, the row test among the failures.
- A request matching an undecided request (TestDedupFoundRequests_ARequestMatchingAnUndecidedOneIsADuplicate) or an open queue entry's request (TestDedupFoundRequests_ARequestMatchingAnOpenQueueEntryIsADuplicate, KeptEntry Q1) comes back as a duplicate and is not kept, so apply opens nothing and adds no entry for it; a decided entry or an entry naming an unknown request matches nothing.
- An applied request matches only while its outcome task (new FoundRequest.Outcome field, round-tripped in TestFoundRequestWithEveryFieldRoundTrips) is open or wip (TestDedupFoundRequests_ARequestMatchingAnOpenOrWipTasksRequestIsADuplicate); a done outcome task is not a duplicate (TestDedupFoundRequests_ARequestMatchingADoneTasksRequestIsNotADuplicate). A handed-back task is done, so it is covered by the done case once its queue entry is no longer open; no separate handed-back marker exists yet.
Out of scope: no tp found apply command yet; opening tasks, the cap, attachment and placement are found-apply-open, found-apply-attach and found-placement, which consume DedupFoundRequests and set Outcome.

tasks.title: Open found tasks within the cap
tasks.description: tp found apply turns Fix-shaped requests into found tasks, blocking first then by arrival, within found_max counted over every found task the file has carried (task answers in, settled tasks out); past it they become open queue entries.
tasks.acceptance:
- with the cap one short, a blocking request filed after a non-blocking one is the one applied (§10 row 'Blocking first within the cap', counts recorded)
- after five found tasks a sixth Fix-shaped request is queued, also after a stop and restart (§10 row 'The cap holds across a restart'); at `found_max=0` it opens a found task
- a Fix-shaped request past the cap is queued and a non-Fix-shaped one goes to the decision unit (round-4 finding 1)
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found apply (internal/cli/found.go, applyFoundRequests under the task-file lock) applies a spec's unapplied requests through engine.PlanFoundApply: duplicates open nothing, Fix-shaped requests (four Fix fields, no question) become open found tasks with origin (id found-<request>, unique against the file) sorted blocking first then by Seq, while CountFoundTasks (tasks with origin in the task file) is below found_max (0 uncapped); every processed request leaves the unapplied state.
- §10 row 'Blocking first within the cap': TestPlanFoundApply_BlockingFirstWithinTheCap (4 found tasks, cap 5, F1 non-blocking then F2 blocking) opens F2 and queues F1. Counts over the 12 PlanFoundApply/FoundApply tests: HEAD 12 pass 0 fail; mutant 'apply in arrival order' (blocking comparison disabled) 11 pass 1 fail, the row test.
- §10 row 'The cap holds across a restart': TestFoundApply_TheCapHoldsAcrossARestart files five requests and applies them in one tp found apply process, then files a sixth and applies it in a second process: it becomes open queue entry Q1 carrying location, reproduction, expected and observed, and the file keeps five found tasks whose schema/references/uniqueness/cycles checks pass in tp validate. Mutant 'count found tasks per run' (count starts at 0 each apply): 6 pass 6 fail, the row test among them. TestFoundApply_FoundMaxZeroOpensTheSixth and TestPlanFoundApply_FoundMaxZeroOpensTheSixth open the sixth at found_max=0.
- Round-4 finding 1: TestPlanFoundApply_PastTheCapQueuesAndANonFixShapedRequestIsUndecided queues the past-cap Fix-shaped request and marks a question-only request and a request with all four Fix fields plus a question undecided for the decision unit; TestFoundApply_AQuestionIsUndecidedAndASecondApplyIsANoOp shows a second apply changes nothing.
- Gate passed via tp gate after 9b103671.
Out of scope: the cap counts found tasks present in the task file, so tp remove of a found task frees a slot; found-settle-cmd must keep the tasks it makes out of CountFoundTasks (e.g. no origin or a marker). Placement edges, attachment and Finders on queue entries are left to found-placement, found-apply-attach and finder-waits.

tasks.title: Attach requests inside an open task
tasks.description: A request whose location falls inside an open spec task's files opens nothing, does not count against the cap, and is attached to that task as a note shown by tp show and the brief; that task is its outcome.
tasks.acceptance:
- a request inside an open task's files opens no task and shows on that task in `tp show` and its brief
- the attachment does not change the cap count
- the closure states whether a request inside an open found task's files attaches, with a test (round-4 finding 3)
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found apply attaches a request whose location falls in an open task's touches (not the finder, status open) to that task as a found_notes entry; it opens no task and does not count against found_max (c16b1127 and e9cb16da tests, landed here).
- found_notes is managed: tp set refuses it; tp show and tp brief (json, text, --compact) list attached notes.
- A request in an open found task's origin location opens its own task: a found task's files are its touches, which apply does not write.
Landed by hand after the driver's integration hit a brief.go conflict with found-brief (both added one BriefTask field; both kept). Out of scope: the §4 placement edge for an attached blocking request; REFERENCE.md for origin/found_notes is the docs task's.

tasks.title: Place found tasks on the finder's edge
tasks.description: Apply adds at most one edge: a non-blocking found task depends on its task finder (an audit finder adds none); a blocking request makes the finder depend on its outcome; an edge that would close a cycle becomes an open queue entry whose question names the cycle.
tasks.acceptance:
- a non-blocking found task lists the finder in `depends_on`; one from an audit row lists nothing
- after a blocking request the finder lists the found task in `depends_on`; a blocking duplicate's finder depends on the kept task
- a blocking edge that would close a cycle adds no edge and opens a queue entry naming the cycle (round-4 finding 14)
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found apply places found tasks on the finder's edge (spec §4): newFoundTask gives a non-blocking found task depends_on [finder task]; an audit-row request (no finder task) gets depends_on []. Engine: TestPlanFoundApply_ANonBlockingFoundTaskDependsOnItsFinder; CLI end-to-end: TestFoundApply_PlacesFoundTasksOnTheFindersEdge (found-f1 depends_on [t1]). Mutant dropping the deps block fails 3 tests.
- A blocking request with a task outcome (its found task, the attached open task, or a duplicate's kept task) adds plan.Edges {finder -> outcome}, written by addFoundEdges under the task-file lock (engine.placeFoundRequests). CLI end-to-end: t1 depends_on [found-f2] after a --blocks request, tp validate cycles/references pass. Blocking duplicate and blocking attachment are proven on the plan in internal/engine only (TestPlanFoundApply_ABlockingDuplicatesFinderDependsOnTheKeptTask, ..._OnlyABlockingAttachmentAddsAnEdge); an existing edge is not added twice (mutant removing the guard fails that test).
- A blocking edge that would close a cycle (BFS over depends_on, existing plus batch tasks) adds no edge and appends an open queue entry whose question names the cycle with the outcome task (e.g. 'finder -> found-f1 -> finder'), carrying the Fix fields and Finders [finder]; the request keeps its outcome (round-4 finding 14). Engine only: TestPlanFoundApply_ABlockingEdgeThatClosesACycleQueuesInstead, ..._TheCycleCheckFollowsLongerPaths. Finder status/attempt handling and waiting are left to finder-waits. Gate green via tp gate on the rebuilt binary.

tasks.title: Make a blocked finder wait on its request
tasks.description: A blocking request with no task outcome makes its finder wait, open and not ready, until a task outcome, a conforms answer, or a settled entry; apply never moves a wip finder whose unit is still running.
tasks.acceptance:
- after a blocking request that becomes a queue entry, the finder is open and not in `tp next`'s ready set; once the entry is rejected it is ready
- §10 row 'An entry holds only its finders': one open entry holding one finder and one unrelated ready task; counts recorded
- apply leaves a wip finder under a live claim or running unit unchanged; it returns to open when that unit exits without closing (round-4 findings 7, 11)
tasks.closed_reason:
- An open found-queue entry holds its finders out of the ready set (model.markQueueHolds sets QueueEntry on each finder an open entry names, read with the task file); a blocking request queued past the cap or on a cycle holds its finder, and tp found apply returns a waiting wip finder to open (engine.FoundFindersToReopen, cli reopenFoundFinders via writeFoundPlan's reopen hook) without counting the attempt. TestFoundApply_AQueuedFinderWaitsUntilItsEntryIsSettled: after apply queues F1 as Q1 the finder t1 is open, tp ready --ids is [t3] and tp next --peek offers t3; after Q1 is rejected the ready set is [t1 t3].
- Section 10 row 'An entry holds only its finders': TestReady_AnEntryHoldsOnlyItsFinders (one open entry holding 'finder', one unrelated open task 'other'; ready set is [other]). Counts over the five finder-waits cli tests: at HEAD 5 pass, 0 fail; under the mutant 'mark every open task waiting while an entry is open' (built in a scratch worktree) 2 fail (the row test and the queued-finder test), 3 pass.
- Apply leaves a wip finder under a live spawn claim, the calling implement unit (TP_UNIT_KIND/TP_UNIT_ID) or a live run's main-tree unit unchanged, and a later apply after that unit exits returns it to open (round-4 findings 7, 11): TestFoundApply_LeavesAClaimedFinderWipUntilItsClaimIsGone, TestFoundApply_LeavesTheCallingUnitsFinderWip, TestFoundApply_LeavesALiveRunUnitsFinderWip; engine selection in TestFoundFindersToReopen_ReturnsOnlyAWaitingFinderNoUnitHolds.
- The earlier attempt's integration failed on a cherry-pick conflict with tp found answer's shared writeFoundPlan; resolved by giving writeFoundPlan an optional reopen hook (tp found answer passes nil). Gate green via tp gate (passed: true).

tasks.title: Apply requests after every run unit
tasks.description: tp run applies requests after every unit, after the round is recorded for audit units; a unit that filed a blocking request and exits without closing returns to open without spending an attempt.
tasks.acceptance:
- a run whose implement unit files a request ends with the found task in the file
- §10 row 'A blocking placement spends no attempt': counts recorded
- `tp found apply` skips the requests of an audit round not yet recorded, so an audit unit's requests are applied only after its round is recorded (round-5 finding)
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp run applies found requests after every unit: DriverOptions.ApplyFound (cli applyFoundFunc, tp found apply's own applyFoundRequests with the driver naming the still-running units) runs after record() in attemptUnits and the pool's exited; TestRunCommand_AnImplementUnitsRequestEndsAsAFoundTask has the fake runner's seed unit file a request (TP_FAKE_RUNNER_FOUND_IDS) and the run ends with found-f1 (depends_on [seed]) in the task file, run as the next unit, the request applied; seen red before wiring.
- §10 row 'A blocking placement spends no attempt': a unit whose task apply returns to open is not a failed attempt (failedUnits waiting set; pool exited case reopened[id], no retry). TestRunCommand_ABlockingPlacementSpendsNoAttempt (main tree, run_max_unit_retries=0) runs seed, found-f1, seed with seed's rows both attempt 1 and seed done depending on found-f1; ...InAPool does the same in a rolling pool, the rerun requiring found-f1.txt in its tree. Counts at HEAD 184edaed: 4/4 of the run_found tests pass; under the mutant 'count the exit as a failed attempt' (failedUnits ignores waiting and the pool's reopened[id] case disabled) 2 fail (both row tests), 2 pass.
- tp found apply skips the requests of an audit round not yet recorded: engine.PlanFoundApplyRecorded holds an unapplied request whose finder.audit_round is above the spec's latest recorded audit round (RecordedAuditRound) out of the plan and dedup and keeps it unapplied in the store; TestFoundApply_SkipsTheRequestsOfAnUnrecordedAuditRound sees nothing opened and the request unapplied before round 1 is recorded, then found-f1 opened after.
- A finder rerun in the same pool now starts from HEAD: setAsideUnitBranch renames its earlier unit branch to tp-unit/<cycle>/<run>-<n>/<id> (commits stay reachable, kept by keptUnitBranch) instead of failing worktree add -b on the existing name; seen red with the require-file knob.
Out of scope: tp found add does not stamp finder.audit_round for audit units yet (task audit-files-requests owns it); the hold was tested with a request stored through engine.AddFoundRequest.

tasks.title: Refuse the coordinator's stop with requests unapplied
tasks.description: In a hand-coordinated session the pool's Stop hook refuses the coordinator's stop once while unapplied requests exist, naming tp found apply.
tasks.acceptance:
- with an unapplied request the Stop hook refuses once naming `tp found apply`; with `stop_hook_active` true it lets the stop through
- with no unapplied request it does not refuse
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp pool --stop-hook (the pool's Stop hook) now refuses a coordinator's stop with a block decision naming `tp found apply --file <task file>` while a task file the session coordinates holds an unapplied found request (engine.Pool.Unapplied via ReadFoundRequests at the root tp found apply uses; asked even when the payload carries no background_tasks), and with stop_hook_active true prints nothing; TestPoolStopHookRefusesWhileFoundRequestsAreUnapplied files a request with tp found add, sees the block naming tp found apply, then sees the stop_hook_active payload pass silently. Seen red first (empty hook output).
- With no unapplied request the hook does not refuse for it: the same test sees an empty hook output before any request is filed and no tp found apply in the output after tp found apply ran; the existing TestPool* stop-hook tests still pass.

tasks.title: Brief a found task from its request
tasks.description: A found task's brief carries the request's fields and no spec excerpt, and says its first step is the reproduction and tp found handback when it does not fail for the stated reason.
tasks.acceptance:
- a found task's brief shows location, reproduction, expected and observed, and no excerpt
- the brief names `tp found handback` as the step when the reproduction does not fail
tasks.closed_reason:
- A found task's brief carries task.request {location, reproduction, expected, observed, first_step} in place of spec_excerpt: BuildBrief skips the excerpt for any task with origin (compact or not) and reads the Fix fields back from the description newFoundTask writes (foundTaskDescription/parseFoundTaskDescription in internal/engine/foundbrief.go; a free-form description is shown whole). TestBuildBrief_AFoundTaskShowsItsRequestAndNoExcerpt asserts the four fields in the JSON and text briefs, with and without --compact, and no spec_excerpt against a real spec where a non-found control task with the same source_lines does get one (seen red before wiring); end-to-end: tp found add + tp found apply + tp brief found-f1 --json in a fresh repo showed location x.go:40, reproduction 'go test ./x', expected 'exit 0', observed 'exit 1' and no spec_excerpt.
- The brief's first_step reads 'Run the reproduction first. When it does not fail for the stated reason, run `tp found handback <id> "<why>"` and stop', with the task's id filled in; the same test asserts 'tp found handback found-f1 "<why>"' in the text and JSON briefs. tp gate passed.
Out of scope: tp found handback itself does not exist yet; the brief only names it.

tasks.title: Add tp found handback
tasks.description: tp found handback <id> "<why>" closes a found task as done marked handed back, opens a queue entry holding its request, and moves the finders depending on it to wait on that entry.
tasks.acceptance:
- after `tp found handback` the task is done and marked handed back, and the queue lists its request
- a finder that depended on the task now waits on the entry and is not ready
- handback on a task without `origin` exits 2
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found handback <id> <why> (internal/cli/found_handback.go) closes a found task as done with handed_back true and reason 'Handed back: <why>', and appends an open queue entry built by engine.FoundHandbackEntry holding its request (F1, location, reproduction, expected, observed); TestFoundHandback_ClosesTheTaskAndQueuesItsRequest asserts the task state and queue entry Q1 after apply opened found-f1 from a blocking request.
- Every not-done task depending on the handed-back task becomes a finder of the entry; TestFoundHandback_TheDependentFinderWaitsOnTheEntry: finders [t1], tp ready --ids is [t3] while Q1 is open, [t1 t3] once it is settled.
- A task without origin is refused with exit 2 and nothing written; TestFoundHandback_ATaskWithoutOriginExitsTwo checks exit 2, 'no origin', unchanged task file and empty queue.
- Each test was seen red under its own mutant (HandedBack not set; origin check skipped; finders loop disabled) and green at HEAD; tp gate passed. The earlier attempt's commits were cherry-picked onto main with the command_sides/found/nongoals_surface conflicts against found decide/settle resolved to keep all three commands.

tasks.title: Leave found tasks out of spec coverage
tasks.description: Spec coverage excludes found tasks from its denominator; a task audit still reaches them through their files.
tasks.acceptance:
- spec coverage reports the same figures before and after a found task is added
- a task audit of a found task lists its files
tasks.closed_reason:
- ValidateLineCoverage skips tasks with an origin, so spec coverage leaves found tasks out of its denominator; TestSpecCoverageLeavesFoundTasksOut (engine) and TestSpecCoverageIsTheSameAfterAFoundTaskIsAdded (cli, via tp add + tp validate) assert the coverage block and coverage/line-coverage findings are equal before and after a found task with source_lines is added.
- A task audit reaches a found task through its files: TestTaskAudit_AFoundTaskIsReachedThroughItsFiles closes a found task with a commit touching found.go and asserts the emitted task_audit lists files [a.go found.go] and tasks [t1 f1]. Gate passed via tp gate.

tasks.title: Record decision answers with the quote check
tasks.description: A command records a decision unit's answer to an undecided request: task (Fix fields, reproduction, quote found verbatim whitespace-normalised in the cited file), conforms (quote checked the same way), or human (queue entry).
tasks.acceptance:
- a `task` answer whose quote is not in the cited file is refused and the request stays undecided (§10 rows 'A quote must be in the cited file' and 'The quote check normalises whitespace', counts recorded)
- a `conforms` answer opens no task and appears in the queue's decided list; a `human` answer adds an open entry with the question and alternatives
- a `task` answer is applied like a Fix-shaped request but never as a duplicate of the request it answers; past the cap it adds an open entry
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found answer <request> <task|conforms|human> [--location --reproduction --expected --observed --cite <file> --quote <text>] (internal/cli/found_answer.go, engine.PlanFoundAnswer in internal/engine/foundanswer.go) records a decision answer to an undecided request under the task-file lock then the store lock; a refusal (unknown request, request not undecided, missing Fix fields, bad cite or quote) exits 2 and writes nothing.
- A task answer whose quote is not in the cited file is refused and the request stays undecided: --cite must resolve inside the project to the spec or a CLAUDE.md/CONVENTIONS.md/REFERENCE.md (engine.FoundCitable), and engine.FoundQuoteIn collapses whitespace on both sides and never finds a blank quote. Section 10 row 'A quote must be in the cited file' (TestFoundAnswer_AQuoteMustBeInTheCitedFile): at HEAD the cli set FoundAnswer is 6 pass / 0 fail; under the mutant 'skip the quote check' it is 5 pass / 1 fail, and the failure is the row test. Section 10 row 'The quote check normalises whitespace' (TestFoundAnswer_TheQuoteCheckNormalisesWhitespace, TestFoundQuoteIn_AQuoteSpanningALineBreakIsFound): at HEAD the engine set FoundQuoteIn|FoundCitable|PlanFoundAnswer is 13/0 and the cli set 6/0; under the mutant 'compare raw bytes' the engine set is 12 pass / 1 fail (the row test) and the cli set 3 pass / 3 fail (the row test among the failures).
- A conforms answer opens no task and adds a decided queue entry with answer conforms, cited, quote and the passing reproduction (TestFoundAnswer_AConformsAnswerIsDecidedAndOpensNoTask). A human answer adds an open entry with the request's location, question and alternatives, and a blocking request's entry holds its finder (TestFoundAnswer_AHumanAnswerAddsAnOpenEntryWithTheQuestionAndAlternatives, TestPlanFoundAnswer_AHumanAnswer...). Both move the request to applied, so a second answer exits 2.
- A task answer is applied through PlanFoundApply as a Fix-shaped request: attach, dedup against other requests, the found_max cap and placement all apply. It plans over the answered request alone, now unapplied, so it never matches itself as a duplicate. Mutant 'keep the undecided request beside the answer': engine set 10 pass / 3 fail (TestPlanFoundAnswer_ATaskAnswerIsNeverADuplicateOfItsRequest among them), cli set 4 pass / 2 fail. Past the cap the answer is an open queue entry carrying the quote, cited file and reproduction, and opens no task (TestFoundAnswer_ATaskAnswerPastTheCapAddsAnOpenEntry). FoundQueueEntry gained cited and quote fields; found.go's apply output and writing were extracted to foundPlanOutput and writeFoundPlan for reuse; SKILL.md lists the three answer forms. tp gate passed in this worktree.

tasks.title: Schedule the decision unit in tp run
tasks.description: A decision unit kind takes at most 5 undecided requests and runs when undecided requests exist and no implement unit is ready or running; when only waiting tasks remain it runs first if a request is undecided, then the run stops with no-ready-task if none is ready.
tasks.acceptance:
- with undecided requests and no ready implement unit, the run spawns one decision unit carrying at most 5 requests
- with only waiting tasks and no undecided request, the run stops with `no-ready-task` without spawning a decision unit
- the decision unit's prompt says it never makes a rule-9 decision and answers `human` when in doubt
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp run schedules a decision unit (new kind "decision", brief `tp found decide <ids>`) when undecided found requests exist and no implement unit is ready or running (implement phase, and first in the audit phase); it carries at most DecisionBatchMax=5 request ids in arrival order, its durable write is none of them still undecided, and an undecided request holds the no-ready-task blocker back. TestRunCommand_UndecidedRequestsSpawnDecisionUnitsOfAtMostFive: six undecided requests behind a blocked task spawn two decision units, F1,F2,F3,F4,F5 then F6, then the run stops (no-units, resume shows no-ready-task); engine TestDecisionUnits_TakeAtMostFiveUndecidedRequestsInArrivalOrder.
- With only waiting tasks and no undecided request (an applied one present), the run stops with no-units and resume reports no-ready-task, spawning nothing: TestRunCommand_OnlyWaitingTasksAndNoUndecidedRequestStopWithNoReadyTask; seen red under the mutant 'schedule a decision unit whenever nothing is ready' (both run tests fail), and TestBuildBlockers_AnUndecidedRequestHoldsNoReadyTaskBack.
- The decision unit's prompt (UnitPrompt via DecisionUnitText) says 'You never make a rule-9 decision' and 'when in doubt, answer `human`', without the finder's tp found add text; tp found decide's brief repeats both: TestUnitPrompt_TheDecisionUnitNeverMakesARule9DecisionAndAnswersHumanWhenInDoubt, TestFoundDecide_BriefsTheNamedUndecidedRequests.
Out of scope: the decision agent (agentByKind, agents/) is left to decision-agent, so the kind runs with the ordinary tool set; tp found decide is not yet in skills/tp/SKILL.md (found-docs).

- engine.AgentDecider plus agentByKind[UnitDecision] make the claude template append --agent tp-decider for the decision kind; TestBuiltinRunner_ClaudeAppendsTheAgentPerKind and TestBuiltinRunner_ClaudeAgentSurvivesExpansion were seen red (no --agent in the decision argv; cli tests failed to compile on the missing constant) before the change and green after; full gate passed via tp gate.
Out of scope: README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.md (Agents 3) still name three agents; that update belongs to found-docs.

tasks.title: Add tp found settle for the person
tasks.description: tp found settle takes a batch and settles each open entry: make a task in that spec's task file (not counted against the cap) or reject with a reason; settling releases the entry's waiting finders.
tasks.acceptance:
- one `tp found settle` call makes a task of one entry and rejects another
- a task the person makes does not count against `found_max`; a finder waiting on it now depends on it
- a rejected entry's finder is ready again
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp found settle --task <entry> --reject <entry>=<reason> (internal/cli/found_settle.go, engine.PlanFoundSettle in internal/engine/foundsettle.go) settles a batch of open queue entries under the task-file lock, all or nothing; TestFoundSettle_MakesATaskOfOneEntryAndRejectsAnother makes task found-q1 of Q1 (entry state settled, task found-q1) and rejects Q2 (state rejected, reason stored) in one call; a bad batch (unknown, non-open, repeated entry, empty reason, missing Fix fields) exits 2 with both files byte-identical (TestFoundSettle_RefusesABadBatchAndWritesNothing).
- A made task carries origin.queue_entry, which CountFoundTasks skips: at found_max=1 after settling Q1 a new Fix-shaped request still opens a found task (seen red with the exclusion removed: it was queued as Q3); the entry's finder t1 gains depends_on [found-q1] and leaves the ready set while found-q1 is open.
- A rejected entry's finder is ready again: in the same test t2 returns to tp ready, and TestFoundSettle_ARejectedEntrysFinderIsReady rejects the cycle-queued Q1 of the foundWaitFixture through the real command, after which tp ready --ids is [t1 t3].
Out of scope: the settled task does not become the request store's outcome, so a later identical request is not deduplicated against it.

tasks.title: Show the queue in resume and payloads
tasks.description: tp resume prints the open entry count and how many tasks wait on them; the converged payload carries the open count; an entry holding no finder changes no phase or --check.
tasks.acceptance:
- `tp resume` prints the open entry count and how many tasks wait on them
- with an open entry that holds no finder, `tp review/audit --status --check` and `tp resume`'s phase are what they would be without it
- the converged payload carries the open entry count
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp resume reports the spec's queue as found_queue {open, holds} (engine.FoundQueueCounts in internal/engine/foundqueuecounts.go; JSON kept under --compact, TTY line 'queue: N open entries hold M tasks'), absent when no entry is open; holds counts each open task an open entry keeps out of the ready set once (Task.QueueEntry), so a done finder waits on nothing. TestResume_PrintsTheOpenEntriesAndTheTasksTheyHold: 3 open entries (two naming one finder, one naming a done task) and a decided one give {open 3, holds 1}.
- An open entry holding no finder leaves the loop verdict and resume's phase unchanged: TestFoundQueue_AFinderlessEntryLeavesTheLoopVerdictAndIsCounted compares review and audit --status --check exit code and the whole payload (found_open aside) before and after writing the entry; TestResume_AFinderlessEntryLeavesThePhase compares phase, next_units, next_action, blockers and round. Seen red under the mutant that gates review converged on a zero open count (review subtest fails), reverted.
- The converged payload carries the open entry count: found_open (present at 0) on review --status/--record and audit --status/--record whenever converged is true (cli addFoundOpen); TestFoundQueue_TheConvergedRecordPayloadCarriesTheOpenCount and the --status test assert 1 open entry counted, the decided one not. tp gate passed.

tasks.title: File out-of-surface audit findings as requests
tasks.description: A Fix-shaped finding outside the spec's surface becomes a request applied after the round is recorded; the row is recorded as out-of-surface under rule 13 naming the request; a found task's commit does not reset the clean-round streak.
tasks.acceptance:
- a Fix-shaped out-of-surface audit finding files a request applied after the round is recorded, and its row's disposition names the request (round-4 finding 9)
- the audit's consecutive clean count is the same before and after a found task closes
- an audit row on an asked item still takes the audit-fix path and files no request
tasks.closed_reason:
- A Fix-shaped out-of-surface audit finding files a request with `tp found add --audit-row <role:item_id>` (internal/cli/found_audit.go, engine.FoundAuditFinder in internal/engine/foundaudit.go): the finder is stamped with the in-flight audit round, so the existing hold applies it only after the round is recorded; at `tp audit --record` (fileFoundAuditRows, after the accept-finding fence and the carry) tp writes the row's disposition from the stored request, {status wontfix, evidence naming it, request: "F1"}, so the row does not dirty the round and no unit accepts a finding. An audit-role unit's plain `tp found add` (a finding that is not a row) is stamped with the in-flight round too. Reading chosen for round-4 finding 9: the row is disposed by tp naming the request, the filer is the audit-role unit mid-round, and "asked" means an item id in the in-flight round's pool for that role (by id, not by location). TestFoundAudit_AnOutOfSurfaceFindingFilesARequestTheRecordNames (held before record, recorded clean unattended, resolved.request F1, then found-f1 opened) and TestFoundAudit_AnAuditUnitsPlainRequestWaitsForItsRound. Counts over the 34 tests of -run 'TestFoundAudit_|TestFoundAdd|TestFoundApply|TestRecordFences|TestAuditRecord': HEAD 34 pass 0 fail; mutant "skip the row disposition at record" 32 pass 2 fail (the row test and the streak test); mutant "no in-flight stamp for a plain audit-unit request" 33 pass 1 fail (the plain-request test). Probed: `tp audit --merge` keeps an unasked row's role and item_id.
- The audit's consecutive clean count reads only recorded rounds' live verdicts, and the filed row's disposition is written at record and never tied to the found task's state: TestFoundAudit_AFoundTasksCloseKeepsTheCleanCount reads consecutive_clean 1 from `tp audit --status` before and after `tp done found-f1`; under the "skip the row disposition" mutant it reads 0 before and fails.
- A row on an asked item keeps the audit-fix path: `--audit-row` naming an item the in-flight round's pool asked that role exits 2 naming the audit-fix path and files nothing, and a recorded FAIL on that item keeps no disposition; a non-Fix-shaped request, a key that is not role:item_id, a round that kept no asked items and no round in flight also exit 2 (TestFoundAudit_AnAskedItemOrANonFixRequestFilesNothing). Mutant "drop the asked-item check": 33 pass 1 fail, that test. Surface pin (nongoals_surface_test.go) and SKILL.md inventory list --audit-row; gate passed via tp gate after 947ed505.
Out of scope: the audit-role unit prompt (engine/runnertemplate.go foundRequestText) names `tp found add` but not `--audit-row`, so a unit will not know to file from its row unless told; REFERENCE.md has no `tp found add` form yet.

tasks.title: Fence task-graph writes inside run units
tasks.description: Under tp run, a unit of any kind but decompose that calls tp add, tp import, tp set depends_on or tp found settle exits 2 naming tp found add.
tasks.acceptance:
- with `TP_UNIT_KIND=implement` and `TP_UNATTENDED=1`, `tp add` exits 2 naming `tp found add`; with `TP_UNIT_KIND=decompose` it succeeds (§10 row 'The fence', counts recorded)
- `tp import` and `tp set <id> depends_on=…` exit 2 the same way under an implement unit; `tp found settle` exits 2 under every unit kind, decompose included (round-5 finding)
- outside a run every one of them behaves as before
tasks.closed_reason:
- Under TP_UNATTENDED with a non-empty TP_UNIT_KIND other than decompose, tp add (including --bulk) exits 2 naming tp found add before reading input (cli fenceTaskGraphWrite/runUnitKind in unattended.go); under TP_UNIT_KIND=decompose it succeeds. §10 row 'The fence': TestFence_TpAddIsRefusedUnderImplementAndLandsUnderDecompose. Counts: at HEAD 7/7 TestFence_ tests pass; under the mutant 'fence keyed on TP_UNATTENDED alone' 4 fail, 3 pass, the row test among the failures.
- tp import and tp set <id> depends_on=... (and a tp set --bulk batch with a depends_on line) exit 2 the same way under an implement unit and pass under decompose (TestFence_TpImportIsRefusedUnderImplementAndLandsUnderDecompose, TestFence_TpSetDependsOnIsRefusedUnderImplement; other fields of tp set stay writable); tp found settle exits 2 naming tp found add under every unit kind, decompose included (fenceFoundSettle; TestFence_TpFoundSettleIsRefusedUnderEveryUnitKind over implement, decompose, review-role, audit-fix).
- Outside a run (no TP_UNIT_KIND, or TP_UNATTENDED with no unit kind) tp add, tp set depends_on and tp import exit 0 and tp found settle keeps its own refusal (TestFence_OutsideARunNothingIsFenced); full gate passed via tp gate.
